morgan: quick heads-up — after landing epilogue fusion for QKV packing (build 1.12.0) our small-seq microbench for seq=16, batch=16 shows ~15% higher p99 latency and ~17% lower throughput. not catastrophic, but consistent across 3 runs :thinking:
perf-bot: nightly-regressions detected: benchmark/fused-attn/seq16-b16 down -17% (compare 2187520000 -> 2187654320)
lee: can you drop the run numbers and the command you used?
morgan: ran bench/fused_attn_simple.py with --model gpt-like --seq 16 --batch 16 --kernels fused_epilogue_qkv --repeat 3
```
# summary (tokens/sec)
baseline (no-epilogue): 3200, 3240, 3188
fused-epilogue: 2700, 2685, 2730
seq=128 (same config): baseline 1500, fused-epilogue 1820
```
ash: interesting — perf profile shows big L2 read amplification only for the small-seq runs when epilogue is on. nvprof snapshot attached to the report: kernel "fused_epilogue_qkv" has repeated prefetch spikes and higher global loads than expected. looks like prefetching loop misses coherence window for small per-thread work.
sam: do we have an easy fallback heuristic? maybe fused epilogue is only beneficial for seq >= 64 or when batch_size * seq_len >= threshold.
lee: agreed. If we can implement a cheap heuristic at kernel selection time we avoid runtime perf cliff and keep gains for long sequences.
morgan: propose heuristic (pseudo):
```
// kernel selection in runtime
if (kernel == FUSED_EPILOGUE_QKV) {
  if (seq_len < 48 && batch_size >= 8) {
    // avoid epilogue fusion: fall back to pack-only + separate epilogue
    use(KERNEL_PACK_NO_EPILOGUE);
  }
}
```
sam: also worth trying a small tweak: reduce prefetch distance for seq<32. might reduce L2 thrash and preserve some fusion benefits.
ash: i ran a quick patch locally: lowering prefetch by factor 0.5 + disabling loop-unroll in epilogue reduces L2 misses and recovers ~8% throughput (still below baseline). so fallback heuristic + prefetch tuning combined should be fine.
lee: can someone add a gated flag so we can A/B in canary? we should collect token-level latency metrics and L2 miss rate counters if available.
morgan: will push a PR with: (1) selection heuristic, (2) runtime flag REDWOOD_FUSE_EPILOGUE=auto|on|off default=auto, (3) perf telemetry tags for kernel_choice and seq_len bucket.
perf-bot: scheduled perf/regression job: run against canary 2187654400 and baseline 2187520000 across seq buckets [16,32,64,128] and batches [1,4,16]. results will post back here.
deploy-bot: canary rollout note: if p99 latency increases >5% for any customer route we'll autostop and roll back. tagging @oncall for visibility.
sam: also add a lightweight unit microbench (in-process) that we run in CI for seq<=32 combos so future PRs don't regress this case.
lee: sounds good. please include the nvprof excerpt and a short annotated flamechart in the PR description.
morgan: ok i'll open PR today and add perf artifacts. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
ash: fyi i left a TODO to check bias/rope fusion ordering — might be an orthogonal cause when we merge bias into the packed qkv path. will follow up separately.
lee: cool. if no objections i'll approve the canary plan once morgan's PR is in.
